items.bold: IRAN offers Oman-side Hormuz passage free of attack as deal proposal.
items.text: A source briefed by Tehran told the Jerusalem Post that Iran could allow ships to sail freely through the Oman side of the Strait of Hormuz without risk of attack — as part of its proposal if a deal is reached. This would be a partial Hormuz reopening via the Omani territorial waters corridor. The Oman side is one of two transit lanes; this would effectively restore commercial shipping to India, Japan, South Korea, and China without full Hormuz control concession by Iran.

assessment.body:
Day 48 close is the most diplomatically loaded evening since the war began.

THE NUCLEAR BREAKTHROUGH — SPECIFIC OPTIONS CONFIRMED
• Pakistan sources tell Al Jazeera: "major breakthrough expected on nuclear front"
• Two concrete HEU disposal options now on table:
  (1) Transfer 440kg of 60% HEU to a third country
  (2) Dilute to 3% civilian-grade uranium (down-blending)
• Both options would effectively remove Iran's near-bomb-grade material
• This is the first time specific disposal options have been publicly confirmed
• Al Jazeera: "Pakistanis are going to be able to convince Tehran"
• Munir expected to travel to Washington after Tehran — to relay Iran's response directly

THE HORMUZ CONCESSION — OMAN SIDE PROPOSED
• Iran offered to allow ships through the Oman side of Hormuz free of attack
• This would restore commercial shipping for India, Japan, South Korea, China
• 20,000 seafarers and hundreds of tankers stuck since Feb 28 could move
• For India: LPG tankers to Mumbai and Kochi via Omani corridor = immediate relief
• Does not concede Iranian control of the strait — politically acceptable to Tehran

HEGSETH'S ULTIMATUM — MAXIMUM PRESSURE CONTINUING
• Pentagon Thursday: "choose wisely... ready at push of a button"
• Gen. Caine: 13 ships turned away (up from 9 on day 1)
• US actively pursuing dark fleet vessels carrying Iranian oil
• Third carrier + thousands of Marines and paratroopers arriving later this month
• Iran command and control "highly degraded" (Hegseth) but "high incentive" for ceasefire

THE STRUCTURAL HEADWIND — IRAN HARDLINERS
• Hardline MPs and state TV: "impossible to accept even one clause"
• Deputy Speaker Nikzad: "We will never give concessions"
• Al Jazeera: three sets of detractors — Tehran hardliners, Washington hawks, Israel
• Israel "does not want a peace deal and wants perpetual war" (Bin Javaid)
• This is why Munir going to Washington is critical — needs Trump political cover

INDIA MARKETS — CLOSE AND OUTLOOK
• Sensex 77,989 (-123): gapped up to 78,730 then faded 741pts on WPI inflation
• Nifty 24,197 (-35): held above 24,000 despite late-session selling
• FII net buyers Rs 666 Cr on Apr 15 — structural shift confirmed
• Wipro Q4: profit +12%, Rs 15,000 Cr buyback at 19% premium — positive for IT
• WPI inflation above expectations: short-term drag but reverses quickly if oil falls
• If HEU options confirmed and second round announced by tomorrow: Sensex 79,000-80,000
• If ceasefire extends and Oman-side Hormuz opens: Brent to $75-80, Sensex 82,000+

CEASEFIRE: APRIL 22 — 6 DAYS
• Scenario A (~70%): HEU deal framework + Oman-side passage + ceasefire extension → Brent $68-75, Sensex 82,000-88,000, rupee to 90-91
• Scenario B (~20%): Lebanon blocks deal, ceasefire lapses Apr 22 → Brent $120-130, Nifty tests 22,000
• Scenario C (~10%): Partial deal — nuclear freeze only, Hormuz disputed → Sensex 79,000-82,000, Brent $85

VERDICT: The nuclear options and Hormuz concession are the two things the markets have been waiting for since Feb 28. If Munir successfully relays Iran's acceptance of either HEU option to Washington before April 22, this war ends. Watch the next 72 hours. India is one Munir phone call from the biggest market rally since 2021.
